A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoGPA and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Retained experiments and qualitative panels can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, a human preference study, computational measurements, and training-step ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds optimization, robustness, out-of-distribution, and Wan2.2 evaluations.

M1.justification: Eq. 12 revises the preference-score formulation from MSE + LPIPS to MSE + λ LPIPS. This introduces explicit weighting, but λ is unspecified, so an implemented weighting change cannot be established. The reconstruction, preference construction, and DPO/LoRA procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on WebVid and dynamic Panda-70M videos, extending beyond the retained DL3DV-based coverage. Appendix G additionally evaluates scripted static-scene camera-motion prompts, previously used for preference construction, as an explicit test scenario alongside natural captions.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain the base models, SFT, Epipolar-DPO, and GeoVideo. New Table 8 adds SFT on preference winners and sequential SFT followed by DPO as comparison strategies against direct DPO. Extending existing comparators to WebVid does not itself change their membership.

E3.justification: Table 1 now specifies Depth Anything V3 for reprojection evaluation, distinct from the VGGT-based preference construction described in both versions. New protocols introduce scene/motion metrics, 100-video WebVid and Panda-70M evaluations, controlled preference-label flips, and Wan2.2 testing. Wan's natural-caption and scripted-prompt evaluations use different geometric backbones, limiting direct comparisons between those regimes.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of scene-detail and motion preservation, winner-only SFT versus DPO, sequential SFT–DPO, agreement among geometric backbones, and tolerance to 10–20% flipped preference labels. OOD and Wan prompt-regime tests further examine generalization boundaries. The earlier training-duration, computational-scaling, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Table 6 introduces central-value ± spread reporting for scene and motion metrics, whereas v1 reports point estimates. The meaning of the ± quantities is unspecified. No additional repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 extensively revises geometric results under the newly specified evaluator: VideoGPA's I2V 3DCS changes from 0.638 to 0.483, and its CogVideoX T2V MVCS advantage becomes a 0.953 tie with Epipolar-DPO. These are revised evaluations, not established same-setting gains. New results include Panda-70M's 64.0% overall VideoReward win rate and multiple robustness comparisons. Existing main-table VideoReward and human-study results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Eq. 12 generalizes the reconstruction-score definition by introducing an LPIPS coefficient λ. The existing DPO derivation, geometric projection equations, and motion-filtering mathematics remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of data-efficient, self-supervised geometric preference alignment improving video consistency while preserving generation quality. Additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendices D–G add explanations concerning preservation of scene complexity, SFT-induced optimization barriers, geometric-backbone agreement, and robustness/generalization. The Wan discussion newly qualifies benefits as prompt-regime dependent. Appendix H also replaces the earlier description of backpropagating geometric feedback with the more accurate description of using it as a ranking criterion.

D1.justification: v2 specifies evaluation-backbone variants and makes the main-text 1,500-step CogVideoX1.5 schedule agree with the unchanged appendix training table. It removes the explicit front-page project URL and the checkpoint-ablation note stating that static videos were retained. These documentation changes do not establish altered training budgets or filtering.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for WebVid, Panda-70M, Depth Anything 3, and Chen et al.'s video-content customization work. The related-work organization and positioning of dense reconstruction preferences relative to epipolar constraints and human feedback remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites quantitative discussion, corrects attribution and grammar, updates affiliations and publication front matter, moves the runtime discussion into Appendix C, and reorganizes appendix sections. Most existing methodological and interpretive prose is retained; the added scientific sections do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The appendix gains substantial tabular presentation for scene/motion statistics, optimization controls, backbone agreement, label noise, OOD evaluation, and two Wan prompt regimes. The runtime table moves from the main text into Appendix C. Existing figures and qualitative comparison panels are retained rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The separate DA3 evaluator and added optimization, robustness, and OOD controls strengthen validation beyond v1. However, reporting problems limit the benefit: v2 Section 4.2 gives I2V 3DCS as 0.579 to 0.551 while Table 1 gives 0.485 to 0.483, and the new λ and ± quantities lack clear specifications. The expanded evidence supports a limited net improvement, with unresolved inconsistencies weakening its interpretation and reproducibility.
